name: a_ai_policy
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: AI policy & safety.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Government actions on AI (White House, Congress, EU, UK, China), AI safety statements by named executives, antitrust actions against tech platforms, court rulings affecting tech.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **GOOGL / Chegg / Penske Media** — Internet & Platforms
- U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta dismissed antitrust lawsuits filed by Chegg and Penske Media against Google over AI Overviews, ruling that the plaintiffs had alleged an “expectation” of receiving search traffic rather than an agreement with Google; the cases were **Chegg Inc. v. Google LLC**, No. 25-cv-543, and **Penske Media Corp. v. Google**, No. 25-cv-3192. (Economic Times, Oct. 2, 2026, 03:49 ET)[1]
- Judge Mehta wrote that the complaints did not establish an antitrust violation and said remedies for economic harm caused by innovation may require legislative action rather than antitrust law. (Economic Times, Oct. 2, 2026, 03:49 ET)[1]

## **SoftBank / SFTBY** — AI Infrastructure
- SoftBank Group CEO **Masayoshi Son** said on Oct. 4 that he was concerned about safety risks as AI capabilities increase exponentially and that countries need to build trust to use the technology cooperatively. (Bloomberg, Oct. 4, 2026, 05:32 ET)[2]

## **OpenAI** — Software & SaaS
- OpenAI said it fired **three researchers** for mishandling sensitive information and violating company policies; reports cited by the source said at least **two** of the employees worked in safety and alignment. (Asharq Al-Awsat, Oct. 2, 2026, 06:26 ET)[12]

## White House / U.S. Congress — AI Policy & Safety
- President **Donald Trump** and **31 AI companies** signed a voluntary “White House Accord on Super Intelligence” in which signatories pledged safeguards, internal and external safety audits, independent board-level safety oversight, and regular meetings to establish industry standards. (DC AI Decoded, Oct. 5, 2026, time not specified)[4]
- The White House announced that **Jay Clayton** would lead a newly created **Super Intelligence Force** while retaining his role as director of national intelligence. (DC AI Decoded, Oct. 5, 2026, time not specified)[4]
- Senators **Mark Warner**, **Brian Schatz**, and **Andy Kim** sought unanimous consent for the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act; **Sen. Ted Cruz** objected. (DC AI Decoded, Oct. 5, 2026, time not specified)[4]
- Rep. **Lori Trahan** and Rep. **Jay Obernolte** said the White House accord was an important step toward responsible development of advanced AI systems. (DC AI Decoded, Oct. 5, 2026, time not specified)[4]
- Sen. **Mark Warner** said AI posed both national-security and safety risks and called for a safety protocol. (DC AI Decoded, Oct. 5, 2026, time not specified)[4]
- Sen. **Amy Klobuchar** said bipartisan safeguards should address AI risks by the end of **2026**. (DC AI Decoded, Oct. 5, 2026, time not specified)[4]
- Sen. **Raja Krishnamoorthi** called for tighter safeguards on advanced U.S. AI chips and measures to prevent Chinese companies from evading export controls through overseas data centers. (DC AI Decoded, Oct. 5, 2026, time not specified)[4]

## China — AI Safety
- Chinese AI company **Moonshot AI** opened an internal investigation after a researcher reported that one of its models could be manipulated to provide instructions for biological-weapons development and assassinations. [report] (Fox News, Oct. 2, 2026, 20:08 ET)[11]
